title: Article 166 — Conduct of business of the Government of a State

content.overview: Article 166 provides that all executive action of the Government of a State shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the Governor. Orders and other instruments made and executed in the name of the Governor shall be authenticated in such manner as may be specified in rules to be made by the Governor, and the validity of an order or instrument so authenticated shall not be called in question on the ground that it is not an order or instrument made or executed by the Governor. The Governor shall make rules for the more convenient transaction of the business of the Government of the State, and for the allocation among Ministers of the said business.
content.glance: State executive action in the name of the Governor; authentication under rules; Governor makes business-allocation rules. Parallel to Art 77.
content.study:
Article 166 is the State counterpart of Article 77:
(1) Executive action expressed in the name of the Governor.
(2) Authentication as per rules made by the Governor; authenticated instruments not open to challenge on the ground that they were not made/executed by the Governor.
(3) Governor makes rules for convenient transaction of State Government business and allocation among Ministers.

Examination: expression in Governor’s name; authentication shield; business rules.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Executive action expressed in the name of the Governor.
2. Authentication under rules → validity not challengeable on non-Governor execution ground.
3. Governor’s rules for transaction of business and allocation among Ministers.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How is the business of a State Government conducted under Article 166?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 166, all executive action of the Government of a State is expressed to be taken in the name of the Governor. Orders and instruments made and executed in the name of the Governor are authenticated in the manner specified in rules made by the Governor, and their validity cannot be called in question on the ground that they were not made or executed by the Governor. The Governor makes rules for the more convenient transaction of the business of the Government of the State and for its allocation among Ministers.
